<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VI.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|233}}</noinclude>to him, {{verse|chapter=6|verse=9}}† There is a boy here that hath fiue barley loaues, & tvvo fishes: but vvhat are these among so many? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=10}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore saith, Make the men to sit dovvne. And there vvas much grasse in the place. The men therfore sate dovvne, in number about fiue thousand. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=11}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore tooke the loaues: and vvhen he had giuen thankes, he distributed to them that sate. in like maner also of the fishes as much as they vvould. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=12}}† And after they vvere filled, he said to his Disciples, Gather the fragments that are remaining, lest they be lost. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=13}}† They gathered therfore, and filled tvvelue baskets vvith fragments of the fiue barley loaues, vvhich remained to them that had eaten. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=14}}† Those men therfore vvhen they had seen vvhat a signe {{sc|Iesvs}} had done, said, That this is the Prophet in deede that is to come into the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=15}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore vvhen he knevv that they vvould come to take him, and make him king, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 23. Mr. 6, 46.''}}* he fled againe into the mountaine him self alone.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=16}}† And vvhen euen vvas come, his Disciples vvent dovvne to the sea. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=17}}† And vvhen they vvere gone vp into the shippe, they came beyond the sea into Capharnáum. and now it vvas darke, and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas not come vnto them {{verse|chapter=6|verse=18}}† And the sea arose, by reason of a great vvinde that blevv. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=19}}† VVhen they had rovved therfore about fiue and tvventie or thirtie furlonges, they see {{sc|Iesvs}} vvalking vpon the sea, and to dravv nigh to the shippe, and they feared. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=20}}† But he saith to them, It is I, feare not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=21}}† They vvould therfore haue taken him into the shippe: and forthvvith the shippe vvas at the land to vvhich they vvent.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=22}}† The next day, the multitude that stoode beyond the sea, savv that there vvas no other boate there but one, and that {{sc|Iesvs}} had not entred into the boate vvith his Disciples, but that his Disciples only vvere departed: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=23}}† but other boates came in from Tiberias beside the place vvhere they had eaten the bread, our Lord {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ These wordes do plainly import, that the giuing thankes was an effectual blessing of the bread and working the multiplication thereof.}}∷ giuing thankes. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=24}}† VVhen therfore the multitude savv that {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas not there, nor his Disciples, they vvent vp into the boates, & came to Capharnaum seeking {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=25}}† And when they had found him beyond the sea, they said to him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} answered them, and said, Amen, amen I say to you, you seeke me not because you haue seene signes, but because you did eate of the loaues, and vvere filled. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† {{sup|‖}} VVorke not the meate that<noinclude>{{rh||Gg|perisheth,}}</noinclude>
